name: Lower eyelid retraction surgery

card.summary: A family of eyelid procedures, including spacer grafts, canthal suspension and midface lifting, that raise a low or retracted lower lid to reduce scleral show and give the eye a more almond-shaped look.
card.aka: Lower lid retraction repair; almond eye surgery; lower eyelid lengthening
card.note: Surgical outcomes can be unpredictable and revision surgery is described as difficult; complications can affect comfort and vision.

quick.overview:
Lower eyelid retraction means the lower lid margin sits below its normal position, showing white sclera under the iris and sometimes giving a round, sad or staring look. Surgeons treat it with a set of procedures that lift and support the lower lid, and in looksmaxxing forums the aesthetic version is often called almond eye surgery.

The appearance payoff people describe is less scleral show and a more almond-shaped, tilted eye. The published literature is largely about repairing retraction after blepharoplasty or from thyroid eye disease, so it describes techniques and outcomes in those patients, with a handful of randomized trials comparing graft materials.
quick.how: The surgery is done by oculoplastic or facial plastic surgeons and typically combines elements such as a spacer graft in the back layer of the lid (cartilage, hard-palate mucosa or acellular dermal matrix), release of scar in the middle layer, midface lifting and canthal suspension at the outer corner. Which elements are used depends on the cause and which layers of the lid are deficient.
quick.risks: Reviews describe surgical correction as difficult and unpredictable, and patient dissatisfaction is a recognised issue, so counselling about expectations is stressed. Retraction itself can cause dry eye, irritation and exposure of the cornea. Community threads discuss botched cases and long waits and high costs with leading surgeons.

lead: Lower eyelid retraction is a malposition in which the lower eyelid margin sits abnormally low, exposing sclera between the lid and the iris and widening the eye opening. Lower eyelid retraction surgery is the family of procedures used to raise and support the lid. Its most common medical causes are thyroid eye disease and complications of lower eyelid cosmetic surgery.[1][2]

In looksmaxxing communities the aesthetic version is known as almond eye surgery. Forum users describe wanting less lower scleral show and a more almond or positively tilted eye, and they discuss it alongside canthoplasty, fat grafting and fillers for the eye area. A 2020s forum thread describes a young man with inherited droopy lower lids and scleral show who sought more almond eyes through lower eyelid retraction surgery without a spacer graft.[3][4]

Clinical research on the topic is mostly reviews and technique descriptions, plus a limited number of randomized trials comparing graft materials. Reviews of thyroid-related retraction say that surgical literature consists mainly of descriptions of techniques and uncontrolled studies, and that only one randomized trial was identified in a 2016 review.[5]

chain: Spacer graft, scar release and canthal support lift the lower lid
Less scleral show beneath the iris
Eye reads as more almond-shaped with a firmer lower lid line
angle.text: The procedures raise the lower lid margin and support the outer corner, which reduces visible sclera under the iris and changes the eye's outline. Forum users pursuing almond eye surgery describe this as improving canthal tilt and the look of the eye area.

paras: Lower eyelid retraction is defined as downward malposition of the lower eyelid margin without the lid turning outward, and it presents with scleral show, round or sad-looking eyes, laxity of the lateral canthal tendon and symptoms such as irritation, tearing and incomplete closure during sleep.[10] It may involve deficiency of one or more of the lid's three layers: the skin and muscle, the middle layer, and the back layer of tarsus and conjunctiva.[1]

Diagnosis is clinical and compares lid position with the lower edge of the cornea, often with a measure called margin reflex distance, with values above about 5.5 mm used as a threshold in some descriptions.[1]

A review of post-blepharoplasty retraction describes the standard surgery as combining midface lifting, a posterior lamellar spacer graft and canthal suspension, and reports variable degrees of functional and aesthetic improvement.[2] Canthal suspension procedures, which tighten or reposition the outer corner, are described as an adjunct to lower lid surgery and include open and closed suspension and canthopexy.[6]

Spacer grafts have been made from autologous ear cartilage, hard-palate mucosa, acellular dermal matrix such as AlloDerm, and porous polyethylene (Medpor), and reviews compare graft contraction with each.[7][8][9][11] In thyroid eye disease, retractor release and recession of the inferior rectus have been described, and hyaluronic acid gel has been reported as a temporary expansion option.[12][13][14] Transconjunctival lower blepharoplasty is discussed as a way to reduce the risk of causing retraction in the first place.[15]

Forum users compile lists of surgeons, consultation fees and waiting times, and discuss near-term plans, healing updates and before-and-after cases. One looksmax.org thread ranking US surgeons says the leading surgeons were booked for consultations six to seven months ahead, and a poster in another thread argues that other eyelid procedures are more established than canthoplasty.[3]

Users also note that "lower eyelid retraction surgery" is a broad label covering many variations, citing a retrospective analysis of 21 procedures in 11 patients that combined midface lift, scar release and a thick AlloDerm graft.[4] Discussion threads also cover botched results and whether retraction affects vision.

A randomized trial in thyroid eye disease compared retractor tenotomy with an antimetabolite against scleral grafting for lower lid retraction, and an earlier randomized trial studied a technique to minimise lower lid retraction with inferior rectus recession.[16][17] Randomized comparisons of spacer materials include dermis versus auricular cartilage in a 2025 trial and autologous auricular cartilage versus bovine and porcine acellular dermal matrix spacer grafts.[7][8] A randomized comparison of inferomedial versus balanced orbital decompression analysed changes in eyelid parameters.[18]

Several registered trials address lower lid retraction, including dermis versus auricular cartilage grafts and acellular dermal matrix versus autologous tarsus.[19][20] A 2016 review of Graves lower eyelid retraction found that controlled studies comparing techniques were lacking.[5] A 2000 review of retraction after cosmetic surgery describes its presentation and management.[10]

Retraction after blepharoplasty is described as challenging and multifactorial, with surgical correction difficult and unpredictable and a frequent negative effect on the patient's mood, which is why preoperative counselling about expectations is stressed.[2] Persistent retraction can produce dry eye, irritation and corneal exposure.[1] Graft contraction over time has been compared between materials.[9]

timeline.event: Technique and complications of transconjunctival lower blepharoplasty are described in Ophthalmology.[21]
Hard-palate mucosa grafting for lower lid retraction is reported.[22]
Randomized trial of retractor tenotomy versus scleral graft in thyroid eye disease.[16]
Review of evaluation and management of retraction after cosmetic surgery.[10]
Randomized trial of dermis versus auricular cartilage grafts published.[7]

lore.intro: Forum threads on looksmax.org discuss almond eye surgery as a way to change eye shape and canthal tilt, and compare surgeons and costs.[3][4]

claims.claim: Almond eye surgery gives a more almond, positively tilted eye
claims.believers: Users describe wanting less scleral show and a more almond shape and share before-and-after cases and plans for surgery.[3]
claims.experts: Published work focuses on repairing retraction from thyroid disease or prior surgery and reports variable aesthetic improvement after standard surgery.[2]

claims.claim: "Lower eyelid retraction surgery" is a broad term for many different operations
claims.believers: A thread cites a retrospective series of 21 procedures in 11 patients combining midface lift, scar release and AlloDerm graft to show how varied the operations are.[4]
claims.experts: Reviews describe a variety of spacer materials and techniques, with few controlled comparisons.[5]
